title: fix: Error when parsing output if tool name contains non-English characters
body:
# Description

I created a tool with a Chinese name, and after the agent invoked it, I kept getting the error "Could not parse output. Please follow the thought-action-input format. Try again." However, no error occurred during the tool creation process, which made this issue confusing.

```python
llm = OpenAI(model="gpt-4-turbo", temperature=0)

entry_agent = ReActAgent.from_tools(
    [
        weather_tool,
        address_geo_tool,
        web_search_tool,
        gas_knowledge_tool,
        # This tool fails to work because its name is in Chinese
        QueryEngineTool(
            query_engine=kitchen_appliance_agent,
            metadata=ToolMetadata(
                name="厨房电器推荐",
                description="可以根据用户的喜好推荐各种厨房电器",
            ),
        ),
    ],
    llm=llm,
    max_iterations=5,
    verbose=True,
)
```

The root cause lies in the regular expression used in `output_parser.py`, which currently limits tool names to characters in the range `a-zA-Z0-9_`. 

In my opinion, this restriction is unnecessary. Additionally, since the tool name serves as a hint to the LLM, supporting multiple languages would make it more intuitive and versatile.

This PR modifies the regular expression to allow tool names to include non-English characters. The change works as expected in my case. I also added a unit test for this case.



Fixes # (issue)

Error when parsing output if tool name contains non-English characters.

title: [Feature] Add optional timeout to a step execution of a Workflow
body:
# Description

Currently, the execution of an entire Workflow (and its comprised steps) are under a single, overall timeout. However, it may be desirable for some use-cases (e.g., human-in-the-loop) for a single step to be executed up to a specified timeout. This PR adds an optional timeout parameter in the `StepConfig` that is used to execute a step under this timeout.

To specify a timeout for a step, we pass in a float value to the `timeout` param when using `step` decorator (defaults to `None` in which case, the standard async execution is performed):

```python
        @step(timeout=1)
        async def my_step(self, ev: StartEvent) -> NextEvent:
            # do step stuff
            return NextEvent(...)

        # works the same for a sync step
        @step(timeout=1)
        def my_sync_step(self, ev: StartEvent) -> NextEvent:
            # do step stuff
            return NextEvent(...)
```

In execution of the step, if a timeout is reached, then we catch the error and raise the newly defined `WorkflowStepTimeoutError`.

Closes #15894

When streaming and you have return_direct=True for a tool, we do a hacky thing and return an AgentResponse that pretends to be a StreamingAgentResponse

Obviously, this makes mypy unhappy, which is why the assert was added.

But instead, to avoid assertion errors, ignoring mypy is a better option

Fixes https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/issues/15883

title: feat: Add a retry policy to steps
body:
# Description

Steps can likely fail for transient problems like network errors and rate limiting. Currently users have to implement their own retrying logic inside each step that might require one. This PR introduces a built-in retry logic provided by the worklfow directly. LlamaIndex will provide a set of pre-defined and configurable retry policies that are commonly used, but users will be able to implement their custom ones.

Example.
```python

    class CountEvent(Event):
        """Empty event to signal a step to increment a counter in the Context."""

    class DummyWorkflow(Workflow):
        # ConstantDelayRetryPolicy will retry at fixed intervals of 1 second, for a maximum of 3 attempts (configurable)
        @step(retry_policy=ConstantDelayRetryPolicy(delay=1))
        async def flaky_step(self, ctx: Context, ev: StartEvent) -> StopEvent:
            count = await ctx.get("counter", default=0)
            ctx.send_event(CountEvent())
            if count < 3:
                raise ValueError("Something bad happened!")
            return StopEvent(result="All good!")

        @step
        async def counter(self, ctx: Context, ev: CountEvent) -> None:
            count = await ctx.get("counter", default=0)
            await ctx.set("counter", count + 1)

    workflow = DummyWorkflow(disable_validation=True)
    await workflow.run()

# Step flaky_step produced an error, retry in 1 seconds
# Step flaky_step produced an error, retry in 1 seconds
# Step flaky_step produced an error, retry in 1 seconds
# Workflow run successfully!
```

To use a custom retry policy, all it's needed is providing a class with one method called `next()` having the follow signature:
```python
class UnreliableRetryPolicy:
    def next(
        self, elapsed_time: float, attempts: int, error: Exception
    ) -> Optional[float]:
        """Retry in a random number of seconds between 1 and 10, stop if the number of attempts is more than 10."""
        if attempts == 10:
            return None
        return float(random.randint(1, 10))
```
and then passing it to the step
```python
        ...
        @step(retry_policy=UnreliableRetryPolicy())
        async def flaky_step(self, ctx: Context, ev: StartEvent) -> StopEvent:
        ...
```

Todo before considering this PR ready:
- Implement the retry logic for sync steps and stepwise execution
- Add proper testing
- Provide at least an exponential backoff built-in policy

title: fix: stop streaming events when a step raises
body:
# Description

In the typical scenario when you want to stream events from a workflow run:

```py
async def main():
    w = MyWorkflow(timeout=10, verbose=True)
    task = asyncio.create_task(w.run(first_input="Start the workflow."))

    async for ev in w.stream_events():
        print(ev.msg)

    final_result = await task
```

If a step raises an exception for whatever reason, that won't bubble up until the execution path gets to `await task`. Before this PR, the streaming queue was not flushed properly in case an exception occurred, and the code would get stuck in the `async for` forever. Now we properly end streaming in case of error.

Issue reported internally.

title: refact: merge Context and Session to simplify the workflows api
body:
# Description

This stems from a conversation with @logan-markewich where we were trying to draw a line in between responsibilities of Context vs. Session. It turned out there's a lot of overlap between the two, and the resulting API was confusing for the users (when should I use a session? When a context? Why does the context has a session property? ...).

This PR merges Session's functionalities into the Context, that's now responsible for:
- Storing data between step executions (same as before)
- Provide utility methods like `collect_events` (same as before)
- Managing the asyncio runtime (was in the session)
- Sending events to the broker and/or the streaming queue (was in the session)

This comes at the expenses of the "private" data storage. Before, since each step had its own context instance, a step could store data in the context so that it was not accessible by any other step, by passing a `make_private` flag to the `ctx.set()` method. Now that the context is unique "per run" and not anymore "per step", "private" storage is not possible and it's up to the steps to store data under a key that's unique enough to prevent clashes.

These changes are not breaking:
- `ctx.session` still works but it returns the context instance now. Users relying on`ctx.session.send_event` won't notice the change and their code will keep running with a deprecation warning.
- `ctx.set(make_private=True)` is now a no-op that emits a deprecation warning.

title: Add KuzuPropertyGraphStore
body:
# Description

This PR adds support for `KuzuPropertyGraphStore` that allows users to leverage a [Kùzu](https://kuzudb.com/) graph database backend.

Kùzu implements a structured property graph model, which means that there are node and relationship tables, whose names and overall structure are decided beforehand via the `validation_schema`. title: doc: Duplicate Argument Passed to delete_ref_doc
body:
# Description

Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed. Please also include relevant motivation and context. List any dependencies that are required for this change.

In `llama_index.core.indices.base.py`, the `update_ref_doc` method is defined as follows:

```python
def update_ref_doc(self, document: Document, **update_kwargs: Any) -> None:
    """Update a document and its corresponding nodes.

    This is equivalent to deleting the document and then inserting it again.

    Args:
        document (Union[BaseDocument, BaseIndex]): document to update
        insert_kwargs (Dict): kwargs to pass to insert
        delete_kwargs (Dict): kwargs to pass to delete
    """
    with self._callback_manager.as_trace("update"):
        self.delete_ref_doc(
            document.get_doc_id(),
            delete_from_docstore=True,
            **update_kwargs.pop("delete_kwargs", {}),
        )
        self.insert(document, **update_kwargs.pop("insert_kwargs", {}))
```

In the current implementation, `delete_ref_doc` is already called with `delete_from_docstore=True`. However, if `update_kwargs` contains:

```python
update_kwargs = {
    "delete_kwargs": {
        "delete_from_docstore": True
    }
}
```

This ultimately results in:

```python
self.delete_ref_doc(
    document.get_doc_id(),
    delete_from_docstore=True,
    delete_from_docstore=True
)
```

#### Impact:

This redundant argument passing could lead to errors like:

```
TypeError: delete_ref_doc() got multiple values for argument 'delete_from_docstore'
```

feature: allow concurrent runs of the same workflow instance
body:
# Description

Move the data structures used to implement the workflow runtime into a new object `WorkflowSession`, decoupling it from `Workflow` and allowing mulitple instance of the runtime (read: concurrent `run()`s).

Example:
```py
class DummyWorkflow(Workflow):
    @step()
    async def step(self, ev: StartEvent) -> StopEvent:
        return StopEvent(result=ev.number * 2)

workflow = DummyWorkflow()
results = await asyncio.gather(
    workflow.run(number=3), workflow.run(number=42), workflow.run(number=-99)
)
```

Fixes https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/issues/15455

Note this moves `self.send_event()` to `ctx.session.send_event()` and I couldn't find a way to keep the old one, so the PR is to be considered breaking.

title: Add MariaDB vector store integration package
body:
# Description

Recently, the popular relational database MariaDB added vector search functionality ( [source](https://mariadb.org/vector-preview/) ).
As the article mentions, the MariaDB vector search implementation is not final and still in development/preview/alpha, but I believe that once an integration here is available it would be much easier to adapt it to any upcoming changes. 
And despite the early stage, it seems to work pretty well - both in my tests and [in benchmarks](https://mariadb.com/resources/blog/how-fast-is-mariadb-vector/).
There is only a small caveat - one of the queries in the integration here had to be designed specifically to work around a [MariaDB bug](https://jira.mariadb.org/browse/MDEV-34774) which is expected to be addressed in the near future.

That's why I think that it's worth adding the MariaDB vector store as a LlamaIndex integration so that more people can easily explore it.

OpenAI needs opt-in arguments to enable streaming token counts

```
llm = OpenAI(
    model="gpt-4o-mini", 
    additional_kwargs={"stream_options": {"include_usage": True}}
)

This PR fixes this by removing stream options from kwargs if streaming isn't enabled. So now you can set it on the LLM, and use streaming or non-streaming ,methods, and not run into errors

title: Fix persisting and loading methods to use correct JSON format
body:
# Description

The existing `persist()` method of SimpleChatStore saves a JSON string, not a JSON object, therefore tools for working with JSON files will not work on the generated persist files. The current `from_persist_path()` also expects a JSON sting. 

This PR fixes that issue so that the saved file is indeed JSON. 

**Steps for reproduction** 

Code:
```python
from llama_index.core.memory import ChatMemoryBuffer
from llama_index.core.storage.chat_store import SimpleChatStore
from llama_index.core.chat_engine import SimpleChatEngine

chat_store = SimpleChatStore()

chat_memory = ChatMemoryBuffer.from_defaults(
    token_limit=3000,
    chat_store=chat_store,
    chat_store_key="user1",
)

chat_engine = SimpleChatEngine.from_defaults(memory=chat_memory)
response = chat_engine.chat("What's up?")

chat_store.persist(persist_path="chat_store.json")
```

Contents of `chat_store.json`:
```json
"{\"store\": {\"user1\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"What's up?\", \"additional_kwargs\": {}}, {\"role\": \"assistant\", \"content\": \"Not much from my end. I'm here to help with any questions or topics you'd like to discuss. How about you? What's on your mind today?\", \"additional_kwargs\": {}}]}, \"class_name\": \"SimpleChatStore\"}"
``` 

Expected contents of `chat_store.json`:
```json
{"store": {"user1": [{"role": "user", "content": "What's up?", "additional_kwargs": {}}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "Not much from my end. I'm here to help answer any questions or chat about a topic you're interested in. How about you? What's on your mind today?", "additional_kwargs": {}}]}, "class_name": "SimpleChatStore"}
```

title: Fix incorrect type in OpenAI token usage report
body:
Corrects an incorrect type assumption when extracting OpenAI token usage reported in the response from (a)client.chat.completions.create.

The response is actually a ChatCompletion or ChatCompletionChunk, which are pydantic objects [1]. The _get_response_token_counts assumed that the response is a dict, with a fallback of not returning anything if the response was anything other than a dict. Because of the fallback, the incorrect type assumption didn't result in an error, but did result in missing token counts. The extracted token counts are returned as additional_kwargs in the ChatResponse.

[1] https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/3d780f260a1d26ab612dde0f870db114a42273bd/src/openai/types/chat/chat_completion.py#L76

Closes: #15523

title: feat: Allow streaming events from steps
body:
# Description

Allow users to consume a stream of events produced by steps during a workflow execution.

Fixes #15394 

Main takeaways:
- We expose the API to stream events from steps through the session instance: `ctx.session.write_stream_event(ev)`
- We expose the events to the user through a method of the workflow: `wf.stream_events()`
- If the workflow was `run` more than once, streaming will produce a meaningful error

Alternatives:
- We expose the API to stream events from steps through a built-in "service", depending on [this ongoing PR](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/pull/15325)
- We expose the API to stream events through `self` (this won't work for unbound steps implemented as free functions)

Further development
- We might introduce "topics" in the stream of events, so that consumers can filter what to get in case multiple steps are streaming data: `async for llm_ev in wf.stream_events(topic="llm")`
- If we let users manage sessions explicitly, we can support streaming from multiple `workflow.run`s at the same time.

Example:
```py
class StreamingWorkflow(Workflow):
    @step
    async def chat(self, ctx: Context, ev: StartEvent) -> StopEvent:
        llm = OpenAI()
        messages = [
            ChatMessage(
                role=MessageRole.SYSTEM,
                content="You are a pirate with a colorful personality",
            ),
            ChatMessage(role=MessageRole.USER, content="Who is Paul Graham?"),
        ]
        gen = await llm.astream_chat(messages)
        async for resp in gen:
            # Allow the workflow to stream this piece of response
            ctx.session.write_stream_event(Event(msg=resp.delta))

        return StopEvent(result=None)


#
# in a main loop
#
wf = StreamingWorkflow()

# run the workflow in the background instead of awaiting it
r = asyncio.create_task(wf.run())

# consume events possibly produced by steps in the workflow
# the loop will exit when the workflow is done in any case
async for ev in wf.stream_events():
    print(ev.msg)

# await the workflow result and access its results as usual
await r

title: Enhance (Qdrant) hybrid/sparse search support
body:
# Description
This PR gives more explicit control over sparse_embeddings to the developer of RAG applications. The motivation is provided in [this issue](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/issues/16717) and the PR directly adapts the `QdrantVectorStore`. Other `VectorStore`s  that support hybrid retrieval will need to be adapted.

This PR aims at enhancing the useablility of the Qdrant hybrid search functionality by adding sparse embedding fields to both the `VectorStoreQuery` and `QueryBundle` and using the provided sparse embedding rather than recomputing it.

Additionally the `sparse_embedding` field is added to the `BaseNode` class and if set, used by the `QdrantVectorStore.add` method rather than recomputing it.

Along with the described changes, a larger refactoring reduces code duplication for the `QdrantVectorStore.{query, aquery}` and enhances readability. The `add` method got a minor rework, too.

## Use Case
If working with (a subclass of) the QueryFusionRetriever and multipe retrievers (that use the same embedding models), the query embedding would be calculated more than once per embedding string. Caching won't help as the embeddings are generally calculated asynchronously. To avoid the resource overhead of duplicate computation, passing the precompted embeddings was possible for dense embeddings already.

## Implementation
The commits within this PR should be self-explanatory and well-structured. The main changes are:
- Introduction of a helper function that either uses the provided sparse embedding or calculates the sparse embedding as before
- using `self._{a}client.search_batch` also in the default case to enable building the requests that shall be sent step-by-step and thus reduce the number of cases
- Removing the async evaluation of `await self.asparse_vector_name()` by precomputing it in `__init__`
- Passing down `hybrid_top_k` from the `VectorIndexRetriever` kwargs to the `QueryBundle` (as done with `_sparse_top_k`)
- Reducing line count by roughly 160 LOC through removal of duplication

## Type of Change
In principle, this is a change to the QdrantVectorStore but as the additional fields in `QueryBundle` and `VectorStoreQuery` are required, a parallel version bump of llama-index-core (and specification in the requirements) will be necessary. The type of changes made are:

title: feat: workflow services (aka nested workflows)
body:
Tracking issue: [15347](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/issues/15347)

# Description

First draft to collect UX feedback around a new feature to introduce workflows dependency. We want to be able to call `ServiceWorkflow` from `DummyWorkflow`.

This PR implements the following syntax:

```py
class ServiceWorkflow(Workflow):
    """This wokflow is only responsible to generate a number, it knows nothing about the caller"""
    @step()
    async def generate(self, ev: StartEvent) -> StopEvent:
        return StopEvent(result=42)


class NumGenerated(Event):
    """To be used in the dummy workflow below"""
    num: int


class DummyWorkflow(Workflow):
    """
    This workflow needs a number, and it calls another workflow to get one.
    A service named "service_workflow" must be added to `DummyWorkflow` for 
    the step to be able to use it (see below).
    This step knows nothing about the other workflow, it gets an instance 
    and it only knows it has to call `run` on that instance.
    """
    @step()
    async def get_a_number(self, service_workflow: ServiceWorkflow, ev: StartEvent) -> NumGenerated:
        # the name of the param, `service_workflow`, must match the name of a service that was added
        # to this workflow with `wf.add_services()`
        res = await service_workflow.run()
        return NumGenerated(num=int(res))

    @step()
    async def multiply(self, ev: NumGenerated) -> StopEvent:
        return StopEvent(ev.num * 2)


async def main():    
    wf = DummyWorkflow()
    # We are responsible for passing the ServiceWorkflow instances to the dummy workflow
    # and give it a name, in this case "service_workflow"
    wf.add_services(service_workflow=ServiceWorkflow())
    res = await wf.run()
    print(res)
```

title: Pydantic V2 (llama-index-core)
body:
# Description

Migrating `llama-index-core` to Pydantic V2. (See [migration guide](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/migration/#migration-guide).)

Resolves #15329 

## Main Changes

- Serialization and Validation of Custom Types (JSON Schema Generation)
- Serialization of Subclasses
- Ordering of `PrivateAttr` and `super().__init__()`
- Other Simple Fixes

### Serialization and Validation of Custom Types

Oftentimes we have types that are not subclasses of Pydantic `BaseModel` that require serialization and validation logic when mixed with `BaseModel`'s. For example: `CallbackManager` and `BaseOutputParser` are not `BaseModel` but they are often used as fields within a class that does inherit from `BaseModel`. In these cases we need to provide the serialization/validation logic to these custom types. There are more than one way to do that, the first way is to implement the `__get_pydantic_core_schema__` and `__get_pydantic_json_schema__`. The snippet below should work for any class, though we can add additional validation/serialization logic if we want here too.

```python
    @classmethod
    def __get_pydantic_core_schema__(
        cls, source: Type[Any], handler: GetCoreSchemaHandler
    ) -> CoreSchema:
        return core_schema.any_schema()

    @classmethod
    def __get_pydantic_json_schema__(
        cls, core_schema: CoreSchema, handler: GetJsonSchemaHandler
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        json_schema = handler(core_schema)
        return handler.resolve_ref_schema(json_schema)
```

The other way to provide serialization and validation is by using `Annotated` and a `WithJsonSchema`:

```python
MessagesToPromptCallable = Annotated[
    Optional[MessagesToPromptType],
    WithJsonSchema({"type": "string"}),
]
```

We should use this for lighter classes that require serialization/validation logic to make Pydantic happy — these aren't meant to be subclassed. 

For serialization (i.e., `model_dump()`, or priorly `dict()`), we can customize using the `model_serializer` decorator:

```python
    @model_serializer(mode="wrap")
    def custom_model_dump(self, handler: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        data = handler(self)
        data["class_name"] = self.class_name()
        return data
```

This is actually what you need to use to properly handle serialization of nested classes (see references: [1](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/8792) and [2](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77007885/pydantic-v2-model-validatormode-wrap-how-to-use-modelwrapvalidatorhandl)).

You can also customize the serialization logic of existing `BaseModel` types with `Annotation`'s as well via `WrapSerializer`. An, example use-case of this would be if you wanted to add `class_name` to the json schema:

```python
def add_class_name(value: Any, handler, info) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    partial_result = handler(value, info)
    if hasattr(value, "class_name"):
        partial_result.update({"class_name": value.class_name()})
    return partial_result

llm_predictor = Annotated[LLMPredictorType, WrapSerializer(add_class_name)]
```

### Serialization of Subclasses

Unlike in V1 serializing a type will only include the fields of the annotated type (see [here](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/serialization/#subclass-instances-for-fields-of-basemodel-dataclasses-typeddict)). This can be a big problem for us as we have built around having full serialization of fields.

For example:

```python
class NodeWithScore(BaseComponent):
    node: BaseNode
    score: Optional[float] = None
```

In `V1` serializing `NodeWithScore` will include all of the fields of the `node`. As a concrete example, if `node` is a `TextNode` type, then the serialization of `NodeWithScore` would include the `text` attribute of the `node`.

However, in `V2` this is not the behaviour. Only the fields of `BaseNode` type (i.e., the annotated type in the class definition of `NodeWithScore`) would be included. The fix (as described [here](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/7093#issuecomment-1679621606
)) would be to use the `SerializeAsAny`:

```python
from llama_index.core.bridge.pydantic import SerializeAsAny

class NodeWithScore(BaseComponent):
    node: SerializeAsAny[BaseNode]
    score: Optional[float] = None
```


### Ordering of `PrivateAttr` and `super().__init__()`

In Pydantic V2, the ordering of setting private fields and calling the `super().__init__()` is more restrictive. Specifically, we need to initialize the model first before setting the private attr.

```python

class MyModel(BaseModel)
    _private_param = PrivateAttr()
    param: str

    def __init__(self, param, private_param):
         super().__init__(param=param)
         self._private_param = private_param
```

### Other Simple Fixes

The other simple fixes that we had to make represent simple method name changes: 

-`schema` to `model_json_schema`
- `dict` to `model_dump`
- `validator` to `field_validator`
- `root_validator` to `model_validator`
- `allow_population_by_field_name` to `populate_by_name`

title: fix: children nodes not carrying metadata from source nodes
body:
when running 2 node parsers the metadata is being lost

reproducible example:

```py
from os import path

from llama_index.core.ingestion import IngestionPipeline
from llama_index.core.node_parser import MarkdownNodeParser, SentenceSplitter
from llama_index.core.schema import Document

current_dir = path.dirname(path.realpath(__file__))

sample_pdf_path = path.join(current_dir, "apple_2023.txt")

with open(sample_pdf_path, "r") as f:
    documents = [Document(text=f.read())]

pipeline = IngestionPipeline(
    documents=documents,
    transformations=[
        MarkdownNodeParser(),
        SentenceSplitter(),
    ],
)

nodes = pipeline.run()

with open("output.txt", "w") as f:
    for node in nodes:
        f.write(node.get_content(metadata_mode="all"))
        f.write("\n---\n")
```

# Description

`Neo4jPropertyGraphStore.get()` makes assumptions about the current graph which may be wrong, particularly if an existing graph is being used which has nodes that lack an `id` property. The `get()` may construct the wrong `WHERE` clause if both `ids` and `properties` are passed in as arguments.

This fix:
- always check for existence of id property with a `WHERE e.id IS NOT NULL` clause
- allows for both ids and properties to be passed in together

title: Fix bug with storing to MongoDBKVStore for knowledge graph
body:
# Description

This PR fixes a bug with storing a `KG` index struct, which gets created as part of a `KnowledgeGraphIndex`, in a keyval index store that uses a `MongoDBKVStore`. The index struct contains a dict of all the triplet embeddings, among other fields. It was then added to the `MongoDBKVStore`'s collection as a single document, causing a PyMongo DocumentTooLarge error. This PR addresses the issue by splitting the `KG` index struct into separate documents when adding it the `MongoDBKVStore`.

Fixes [#9546](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/issues/9546)

# Description

In the `QueryFusionRetriever`, corrently node text is used to match results from different retrievers. title: feat: Allow None metadata filter by using IS_EMPTY operator
body:
# Description

From what I know, we currently don't support filtering for fields that don't exist in the metadata or have a null value. In reality, indexed data can come from various streams, and differences in metadata happen quite often. It would be great if we could support filtering with null values or allow fields that aren’t available in the metadata to be filtered as well.

So in this PR, I'd like to propose adding a filter: `is_empty(key)` filter - which would match all records that either don't have a key or have a key that is null or empty. This is similar to the `is_empty` filter from Qdrant: https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/filtering/#is-empty

Let me know if you have any other ideas, and I can put together another PR for that!

# 1) Minor Bug Fix
Fixed bug where if allowed_entity_props  or allowed_relation_props are not configured (None by default), the DynamicLLMPathExtractor raises the following error:

none is not an allowed value (type=type_error.none.not_allowed) 
`

# 2) Fixed dynamic llm output parsers which were not working most of the time
I also tried to make the output parsers for the dynamic llm (both with and without properties) as flexible and as robust to inconsistences in LLM output as possible. With weaker LLMs, sometimes the LLM used double quotations mixed with single quotations, and sometimes just single quotations. These weren't properly handled by the very rigid previous output parsers which resulted in empty knowledge graphs despite the LLMs returning an output full of triplets with minor format inconsistencies. 

This should serve as a temporary fix for now, it's better than what was initially here but not perfect as we never know what the LLM might come up with next ^^'

The ideal would be to use PyDantic to define a proper rigid output but I didn't have the time to do it for now.

Here's a notebook showing how the previous output parsers simply didn't work in certain examples vs the new output parsers working on inconcistently formatted LLM outputs (I had to zip it because Github doesn't support .ipynb files yet):

title: Enhancment/qdrant remove default vector name
body:
# Description

Supporting the default vector "" does not add much.

Whether or not the VectorStore is `enabled_hybrid=True` or not, the DENSE_VECTOR_NAME should be the name of the named vector. We shouldn't rely on the default vector name "" and the DENSE_VECTOR_NAME as this distinction doesn't add anything, it just creates configuration issues. 

For example, it makes it difficult to reconfigure the VectorStore with `hybrid=False` as we are now querying the default name "" instead of the DENSE_VECTOR_NAME. So why not just always use the named vector always and avoid this? I believe this approach is more robust.

Fixes # (issue)

These changes fix this issue to ensure that any dense vector created is named the DENSE_VECTOR_NAME and these configuration issues will be avoided.

title: add option to avoid loading nodes into context that has them already
body:
I noticed when running the original version that it was very slow, so I looked in the code and saw that it is trying to populate the storage context docstore again for no apparent reason.
To make it quicker I overrode the build_index_from_nodes in a child class as:

```
class QuickerSimpleKeywordTableIndex(SimpleKeywordTableIndex):
    def build_index_from_nodes(self, nodes):
        """Build the index from nodes."""
        return self._build_index_from_nodes(nodes)
```
    
This helped a lot, so I thought it should be an option in the base class.


This comes in handy when loading the nodes from the storage context, for example:

```
nodes = list(storage_context.docstore.docs.values())
keyword_index = QuickerSimpleKeywordTableIndex(nodes=nodes, storage_context=storage_context, show_progress=True)
```

title: Bugfix: Don't pass empty list of embeddings to elasticsearch store when using sparse strategy
body:
# Description

When using an elasticsearch-based vector store with the `AsyncSparseVectorStrategy`, embeddings do not need to be generated, as they are created within elasticsearch using the ELSER pipeline. In the llamaindex elasticsearch store, when inserting documents we call `embeddings.append(node.get_embedding())` for each node we're attempting to index, resulting in a list of Nones.

This list of Nones gets passed to the elasticsearch vector store [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch-py/blob/3073f9c195c88e6d9ecaadbae6aee05b6a3f2867/elasticsearch/helpers/vectorstore/_async/vectorstore.py#L154) where it erroneously evaluates as truthy, causing the `vector_field` value on the indexing request to be set to `None` instead of being omitted. This, in turn, causes an `illegal_argument_exception`. 

To fix, simply check if the list of embeddings generated for the documents we're indexing is all Nones, and if so, omit the vector argument to the elasticsearch client.

Fixes [#14821](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/issues/14821)

title: Added feature to stream_chat allowing previous chunks to be inserted into the current context window
body:
# Description

When using various RAG pipelines. oftentimes questions such as "Can you elaborate?" or "Can you explain further?" are unable to be answered. This is due to the fact that the embedding model will search for chunks in the documents that match this exact query instead of reusing the chunks from the previous questions, and therefore the LLM will claim that this question is out of context.

To fix this, I maintained a history of the previous chunks fetched from previous queries and used the SimilarityProcessor to ensure all chunks with scores below 0.05 are not added to the context. This ensures that questions such as "Can you elaborate" have empty context windows since all the chunks found have scores of around 0.001. Then, I passed in a list of previous chunks into the stream_chat function as an optional parameter, and if the context window is empty, I insert hose previous chunks into the current context window by editing the context string. 

I am using PrivateGPT, so the code that handles the SimilarityProcessor and the history of previous chunks is handled in PrivateGPT's codebase.

Fixes # (issue)

title: fix unpicklable attributes
body:
A previous series of PRs was made to improve pickling in the library
1. https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/pull/8838
2. https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/pull/8889
3. https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/pull/8986
4. https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/pull/9588

However, the current iteration ALWAYS removes all private attributes, assuming that we have info info to run `init` when reloading the module. This isn't always true, and when things fallback to normal `setstate`, we get some hard to debug issues for users.

This PR attempts to only remove things that need to be removed. Again, we rely on calling `init` when reloading the module, but the fallback to `setstate` will be much safer now.

Fixes https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/issues/14837

# Description

# RAGChecker Integration with LlamaIndex

This PR introduces integration between LlamaIndex and RAGChecker, a comprehensive evaluation framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems.

## About RAGChecker

RAGChecker is an open-source tool designed to provide in-depth analysis and diagnostics for RAG systems. It offers:

- Fine-grained evaluation using claim-level entailment checking
- A suite of metrics covering overall performance, retriever effectiveness, and generator behavior
- Actionable insights for improving both retrieval and generation components of RAG systems

## Integration Details

This PR includes:

1. A new integration function `response_to_rag_results` in `ragchecker.integrations.llamaindex` to convert LlamaIndex query engine outputs to RAGChecker format.
2. A Jupyter notebook demonstrating the integration, covering:
   - Introduction to RAGChecker and its metrics
   - Setup and usage of the integration function
   - Evaluation of LlamaIndex query results using RAGChecker
   - Examples of customizing evaluations with specific metric groups or individual metrics

## Benefits

This integration allows LlamaIndex users to:
- Easily evaluate their RAG applications using RAGChecker's comprehensive metrics
- Gain deeper insights into their system's performance across retrieval and generation tasks
- Identify specific areas for improvement in their RAG pipelines

We believe this integration will be valuable for the LlamaIndex community in developing and refining more effective RAG applications.

title: Add option to include pipeline_id at top level in MongoDBAtlasVectorSearch
body:
## Description
This PR introduces a new feature in the `MongoDBAtlasVectorSearch` class that allows users to add the `pipeline_id` as a top-level field in MongoDB documents, in addition to its existing presence within the metadata.

## Changes
- Added a new parameter `add_pipeline_id_top_level` (boolean) to the `MongoDBAtlasVectorSearch` constructor.
- Added a new parameter `pipeline_id_key` (string) to allow customization of the field name for the top-level pipeline ID.
- Modified the `add` method to include the pipeline_id at the top level of the document when the feature is enabled.

## Motivation
`pipeline_id` is required at top level in document, during retrieval from `llamacloud`, the `pipeline_id` is added as filter.

## Usage
Users can enable this feature as follows:

```python
vector_store = MongoDBAtlasVectorSearch(
    mongodb_client=client,
    add_pipeline_id_top_level=True,
    pipeline_id_key="custom_pipeline_id",  # Optional, defaults to "pipeline_id"
    # ... other parameters ...
)
```

## Testing
To test this change:
1. Initialize `MongoDBAtlasVectorSearch` with `add_pipeline_id_top_level=True`.
2. Add nodes with metadata containing a `pipeline_id`.
3. Verify that the inserted documents in MongoDB contain the `pipeline_id` at the top level.
4. Test with `add_pipeline_id_top_level=False` to ensure backward compatibility.

title: fix: llamaindex agent chat function will lose external args
body:
# Description

This PR fixes a bug that llamaindex agent losing external chat args.

For example, AzureOpenAI chat() supports `user` parameter:
```
from llama_index.llms.azure_openai import AzureOpenAI
llm = AzureOpenAI(
    engine="simon-llm", model="gpt-35-turbo-16k", temperature=0.0
)
messages = [
    ChatMessage(
        role="system", content="You are a pirate with colorful personality."
    ),
    ChatMessage(role="user", content="Hello"),
]
llm.chat(messages, user="my_user_id")
```

However, OpenAIAgent cannot chat() with `user` parameter:

```
from llama_index.llms.azure_openai import AzureOpenAI
from llama_index.agent.openai import OpenAIAgent
llm = AzureOpenAI(
    engine="simon-llm", model="gpt-35-turbo-16k", temperature=0.0
)
agent = OpenAIAgent.from_tools(
    [multiply_tool, add_tool], llm=llm, verbose=True
)
# will cause error
agent.chat("What is (121 * 3) + 42?", user="my_user_id")
```

If an LLM endpoint requires certain argument to start a chat (i.e. some Azure OpenAI enterprise endpoints will only allow whitelisted user id), user will not be able to use llamindex agent.

title: bug in reading files from sharepoint (windows)
body:
# Description
The current code encounters an issue when reading files from SharePoint documents. Specifically, the SharePoint site name is retrieved in a Windows-style format (\\ instead of /), which causes the replacement logic to fail when attempting to extract data from SharePoint site documents. This pull request addresses this issue by replacing occurrences of / with \\ in the file path string.

Issue
When reading files from SharePoint documents, the SharePoint site name is retrieved with backslashes (\\) instead of forward slashes (/). This discrepancy causes the file path processing logic to fail, as it expects the SharePoint site name in the Unix-style format (/). Consequently, the expected replacements and subsequent data extraction do not occur.

Solution
To resolve this issue, the proposed solution modifies the file path construction logic. Specifically, it replaces occurrences of / with \\ in the file path string. This adjustment ensures that the file path constructed aligns with the format returned by SharePoint, thereby enabling successful data extraction from SharePoint site documents.
Before
```
        file_path = (
            str(input_file).lstrip("/").replace(f"{self.sharepoint_site_name}/", "", 1)
        )
``` 
After
```
 file_path = (
 str(input_file).lstrip("/").replace(f"{self.sharepoint_site_name}\\", "", 1)
)
``` 

Fixes # (issue)

### Description

The original implementation of the `aget_response` method in the `simple_summarize.py` file causes the async method to not work properly, leading to IO blocking when using FastAPI to serve LlamaIndex. response = await self._llm.astream(
    text_qa_template,
    context_str=truncated_chunks,
    **response_kwargs,
)

When loading documents with multiple workers (e.g. `SimpleDirectoryReader(...).load_data(num_workers=n)`), if there are multiple pptx files containing images, the workers all use the same hardwired temp-file. This is easily fixed by using a unique temporary filename for images in pptx files.

title: Update ReAct Step to solve issue with uncomplete generation
body:
This solves issue of missing initial words in text when using 'stream' and 'astream'.

# Description

This issue happens when agent tries to answer implicitly(doesn't follow thought-action format) when streaming.
For example user asks agent:
```python
chat_stream = await agent.astream_chat("How are you?")
async for chunk in chat_stream.async_response_gen():
    print(chunk)
```
The expected answer should be implicit answer which is:
_I'm an AI assistant, so I don't have feelings_
But as result we come up with following text:
_AI assistant, so I don't have feelings_
As we can see we miss the _"I'm an"_ part of text. Let's see why it happens.

Problem happens here:
```python
async def _arun_step_stream(
        self,
        step: TaskStep,
        task: Task,
    ) -> TaskStepOutput:
    ...
    for latest_chunk in chat_stream:
          full_response = latest_chunk
          is_done = self._infer_stream_chunk_is_final(latest_chunk)
          if is_done:
              break
    ...
    response_stream = self._add_back_chunk_to_stream(
          chunk=latest_chunk, chat_stream=chat_stream
      )
    ...
``` 
```python
def _infer_stream_chunk_is_final(self, chunk: ChatResponse) -> bool:
    ...
    latest_content = chunk.message.content
        if latest_content:
            # doesn't follow thought-action format
            if len(latest_content) > len("Thought") and not latest_content.startswith(
                "Thought"
            ):
            return True
    ...
```
So, when code starts to iterate through `chat_stream` first 3 chunks that enter to `_infer_stream_chunk_is_final` method are _("I", "'m", "an")_.
And if we will look inside of `_infer_stream_chunk_is_final` method, we see that content _"I'm an"_  length is not greater than _"Thought"_ so all that three chunks will be skipped and missed. 
On the next iteration, content(at that iteration content is  _"I'm an AI"_ and chunk is _"AI"_) exceeds length of word _"Thought"_ and True is returned. And when `_add_back_chunk_to_stream` method is called only last chunk is added to stream(last chunk is _"AI"_), so previous _("I", "'m", "an")_ chunks are skipped and missed.
So, the same applies to `achat_stream`.

As the solution I store first chunks in list(until content does not exceed length of word _"Thought"_), then if case if true(it does not follow follow thought-action format) those missed chunks will be passed to `_add_back_chunk_to_stream` method along with `latest_chunk`.

title: DynamicLLMPathExtractor for Entity Detection With a Schema inferred by LLMs on the fly
body:
# Description
This pull request introduces a new `DynamicLLMPathExtractor` in the `dynamic_llm.py` file, which improves upon the existing `SimpleLLMPathExtractor`. The new extractor offers enhanced functionality for knowledge graph construction by detecting entity types (labels) instead of simply labeling them as "__ entity __" and "chunk", as well as allowing for ontology expansion.

Key improvements:
1. Detects entity types (labels) instead of labeling them generically as "entity" and "chunk".
2. Accepts an initial ontology as input, specifying desired nodes and relationships.
3. Encourages ontology expansion through its prompt design, unlike the strict schema adherence of `SchemaLLMPathExtractor`.

This new extractor provides a middle ground between `SimpleLLMPathExtractor` and `SchemaLLMPathExtractor`, offering more flexibility in knowledge graph construction while still providing guidance through an initial ontology.

title: 🐞 fix(core): fix llama-index-core\llama_index\core\node_parser\text\utils.py error when use IngestionPipeline parallel
body:
# Description

when use IngestionPipeline parallel , the function `split_by_sentence_tokenizer` defined an internal function `split` and return it, but it can't pickle:

```python
def split_by_sentence_tokenizer() -> Callable[[str], List[str]]:
    import nltk

    tokenizer = nltk.tokenize.PunktSentenceTokenizer()

    # get the spans and then return the sentences
    # using the start index of each span
    # instead of using end, use the start of the next span if available
    def split(text: str) -> List[str]:
        spans = list(tokenizer.span_tokenize(text))
        sentences = []
        for i, span in enumerate(spans):
            start = span[0]
            if i < len(spans) - 1:
                end = spans[i + 1][0]
            else:
                end = len(text)
            sentences.append(text[start:end])

        return sentences

    return split
```

I fixed it in two steps:

1. extract `split_by_sentence_tokenizer` internal func `split` to top level
2. use lambda to return it

Fixes #14280

body:
# Description

Enhanced Notion reader with methods to list databases and pages, added retry mechanism for API requests, and improved logging for better debugging.

### New Features

1. **Request with Retry Mechanism**: Added `_request_with_retry` method for retrying requests and handling rate limits.
2. **List Databases**: Added `list_databases` method to list all databases in the Notion workspace.

### Modifications

1. **\_read_block Method**: Now uses `_request_with_retry` for API requests.
2. **query_database Method**: Updated to use `_request_with_retry` and handle pagination.
3. **search Method**: Updated to use `_request_with_retry` and handle pagination.
4. **load_data Method**: Now supports loading from multiple databases via a list of `database_ids`.

### Bug Fixes

1. **Rate Limit Handling**: Improved error handling with exponential backoff in `_request_with_retry`.
2. **Pagination Handling**: Fixed issues in `query_database` and `search` methods for better pagination handling.

### Example Usage

1. **Main Block**: Added examples for listing databases within a workplace.

title: Neo4j vector context retriever bug fix
body:
# Description
Previously, when using the `VectorContextRetriever` with the `Neo4jPropertyGraphStore`, the `VectorContextRetriever`would call `avector_query` to get the `similarity_top_k` nodes and return the list of nodes with the first node being ranked with the highest similarity score, and the last being least similar. However, when we pass the nodes found from `avector_query` to `aget_rel_map`, the nodes returned could be in any order of similarity. So we need to fix this issue. For example, if I have a query: `nodes = retriever.retrieve("Andres Mendez")`, then then resulting node ids from `avector_query` could look like the following: ['Andres Mendez', 'Andres', 'Miguel Mendez', 'Joe Mamma']. But then the results from `aget_rel_map` could provide only the top 30 results from the relationships of Joe Mamma. This is not expected behaviour, as we are querying for Andres Mendez, not Joe Mamma. The issue here is that we don't take similarity score into account when when calling aget_rel_map, but we need to.

Fixes # (issue)
I modified the cypher query in `aget_rel_map` to return results based on the order of the node ids passed into this function. This will preserve the scores of the input nodes in the response of this function.

# Description

Purpose:
Define multiple levels of nested filters (inner_filter1, inner_filter2).

Approach:
The function recursively processes each filter in standard_filters. 
If a filter is a MetadataFilters object, it recursively calls _to_mongodb_filter to generate the MongoDB filter for nested filters. 
If a filter is a MetadataFilter object, it checks if the value is a list and applies the $in operator if necessary. It constructs the MongoDB filter dictionary based on the condition specified in MetadataFilters.

Fixes # (issue)
Allows you to handle complex filter structures with multiple levels of nesting, applying logical conditions ('and' or 'or') as specified.

title: Enhance SlackReader to fetch Channel IDs from Channel Names/Patterns
body:
## Summary

This PR enhances the `SlackReader` class to support filtering Slack channels based on channel name patterns, including exact names and regular expressions. This update makes it easier to specify and retrieve conversations from channels by adding method to get channel IDs using channel names or regex pattern.

## Changes

- **Feature:** Added support for extracting channel ids from channel name patterns (exact names and regex) in `SlackReader`.
- **Enhancement:** Added the `get_channel_ids` method to fetch channel ids from name patterns, these ids can be further used in `load_data` same as before.

- **Bug fixes** 

    - **Error Handling:** If `not_in_channel` error or any other error except `ratelimited` is returned by Slack, The code went into infinite loop of indefinite retries.  Improved handling of the not_in_channel error. The reader now logs this error and breaks the loop, preventing indefinite retries.
    - **Rate Limiting:** Enhanced rate-limiting logic by adding a default retry interval, ensuring controlled retries when the retry-after header is missing.


## Motivation

The existing implementation required channel IDs to retrieve conversations, which could be cumbersome for users who may not have direct access to these IDs. By allowing the use of channel name patterns, this update simplifies the process of specifying channels, especially when dealing with multiple or dynamically named channels.

## Testing

- Verified that channels are correctly filtered based on provided name patterns.
- Ensured that both exact name matches and regex pattern matches are handled appropriately.
- Tested the `load_data` method with various combinations of channel IDs and name patterns to confirm correct functionality.

---

Please review the changes and provide feedback. Thank you!

title: Update output parsing for tool runner in notebook example of using agent
body:
# Description

The example notebook for building an agent around a query pipeline includes executing a `ToolRunnerComponent` as one step of the pipeline. Originally, an observation step containing `str(tool_output["output"])` is added, where `tool_output` is the result of `ToolRunnerComponent.run_component()`. This, however, has the issue that the return value of this function is actually a dictionary:
https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/7d3bb2b502c95e0677013ac935992d4cb1e36d9d/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/query_pipeline/components/tool_runner.py#L82

Converting the entire dictionary to string instead of just the value corresponding to the "output" key is, in turn, problematic. For example, in case that the tool is a query engine, the object stored in "output" would be a `Response`. When directly converting a `Response` into a string, only the final synthesized response would be given. However, when the entire dictionary is printed, the internal representation of `Response` object would be printed instead, which would not only be the final response, but also all the nodes queried. This could easily cause the input to LLM to exceed the context window size.

**Summary for new feature**: Added filters for neo4j_property_graph since they weren't supported previously even though neo4j property graph supports vector queries. So I modified the code path to support vector filters.

**Summary for bug fix**: bug occurs when you provide TextToCypherRetriever with `self.allowed_output_fields=None`. In that case the code path fails in two places:
1. _clean_query_output: python fails on the first condition because you cannot iterate over a none type (so we need to swap these two conditions):

if (
    key in self.allowed_output_fields
    or self.allowed_output_fields is None
):
```

```python
if self.allowed_output_fields is not None:
    parsed_cypher_query = self._parse_generated_cyher(response)

query_output = self._graph_store.structured_query(parsed_cypher_query)
```

)

    index.property_graph_store,
    llm=llm,

)

title: wip: refactor query pipeline agent to use stateful function components
body:
this should be a cleaner UX than the old guide which made users use `AgentInputComponent` and `AgentFnComponent` to define an agentic query pipeline.

Here you can define a query pipeline through a single abstraction `StatefulFnComponent`: 
- no more two separate component classes (which didn't make sense) 
- single state dictionary passed around (instead of both task and step state) 
- use same abstractions as LoopComponent

When you wrap a query pipeline with an agent worker, the `task` and `step.step_state` are injected in the state dictionary of every stateful component. 

This also makes it easier to test the query pipeline used for an agent in isolation. Just initialize the state dictionary of the query pipeline with `task` and `step.step_state`, and do `pipeline.run()`

title: Add tidb knowledge graph store
body:
# Description

This PR implements a new knowledge graph store using [TiDB](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/overview), which stores graph data in a relational database.

Property graph use case example
```
from llama_index.core import PropertyGraphIndex
from llama_index.embeddings.openai import OpenAIEmbedding
from llama_index.llms.openai import OpenAI
from llama_index.core.indices.property_graph import SchemaLLMPathExtractor
from llama_index.graph_stores.tidb import TiDBPropertyGraphStore

graph_store = TiDBPropertyGraphStore(
    db_connection_string="mysql+pymysql://user:password@host:4000/dbname?ssl_verify_cert=true&ssl_verify_identity=true",
)

index = PropertyGraphIndex.from_documents(
    documents,
    embed_model=OpenAIEmbedding(model_name="text-embedding-3-small"),
    kg_extractors=[
        SchemaLLMPathExtractor(
            llm=OpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo", temperature=0.0)
        )
    ],
    property_graph_store=graph_store,
    show_progress=True,
)
```

Older knowlege graph use case example
```
from llama_index.graph_stores.tidb import TiDBGraphStore
from llama_index.core import (
    KnowledgeGraphIndex,
    SimpleDirectoryReader,
    StorageContext,
)

documents = SimpleDirectoryReader(
    "../../../examples/data/paul_graham/"
).load_data()

graph_store = TiDBGraphStore(
    db_connection_string="mysql+pymysql://user:password@host:4000/dbname"
)
storage_context = StorageContext.from_defaults(graph_store=graph_store)
index = KnowledgeGraphIndex.from_documents(
    documents=documents,
    storage_context=storage_context,
    max_triplets_per_chunk=2,
)
query_engine = index.as_query_engine(
    include_text=False, response_mode="tree_summarize"
)
response = query_engine.query(
    "Tell me more about Interleaf",
)
print(response)
```

body:
# Description


Currently, the metadata in the response returned by SQLTableRetrieverQueryEngine is not correctly formatted. The code in issue #14168 results in a reponse with metadata
```
{'779576b4-46c5-4802-904a-5cf8023b7ee9': {}, 'sql_query': 'SELECT city_name, population \nFROM city_stats \nORDER BY population DESC \nLIMIT 1;', 'result': [('Tokyo', 13960000)], 'col_keys': ['city_name', 'population']}

While the expected metadata should be
```
{'779576b4-46c5-4802-904a-5cf8023b7ee9': {'sql_query': 'SELECT city_name, population\nFROM city_stats\nORDER BY population DESC\nLIMIT 1;', 'result': [('Tokyo', 13960000)], 'col_keys': ['city_name', 'population']}}
```
This pull request fix the issue by correctly setting the metadata of the retrived SQL node in `SQLRetriever`

Fixes #14168

title: enable stepwise execution of query pipelines
body:
QueryPipelines are extremely stateful. If another module tries to drive the execution of a pipeline, they will have a hard time doing with without using private methods and reading a lot of source code

Here's a sample of what it looks like

```python
run_state = p.get_run_state(movie_name="The Departed")

next_module_keys = p.get_next_module_keys(run_state)

while True:
    for module_key in next_module_keys:
        # get the module and input
        module = run_state.module_dict[module_key]
        module_input = run_state.all_module_inputs[module_key]

        # run the module
        output_dict = module.run_component(**module_input)

        # process the output
        p.process_component_output(
            output_dict,
            module_key,
            run_state,
        )

    # get the next module keys
    next_module_keys = p.get_next_module_keys(
        run_state,
    )

    # if no more modules to run, break
    if not next_module_keys:
        run_state.result_outputs[module_key] = output_dict
        break

# the final result is at `module_key`
# it is a dict of 'output' -> ChatResponse object in this case
print(run_state.result_outputs[module_key]["output"].message.content)
```

```python
import tempfile
from urllib.request import urlretrieve

from llama_index.core import SimpleDirectoryReader
from llama_index.core.extractors import SummaryExtractor, TitleExtractor
from llama_index.core.ingestion import IngestionPipeline
from llama_index.core.instrumentation import get_dispatcher
from llama_index.core.instrumentation.span_handlers import SimpleSpanHandler
from llama_index.core.node_parser import SentenceSplitter
from llama_index.core.schema import MetadataMode
from llama_index.embeddings.openai import OpenAIEmbedding
from llama_index.llms.openai import OpenAI

handler = SimpleSpanHandler()
get_dispatcher().add_span_handler(handler)

with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() as tf:
    urlretrieve(
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/run-llama/llama_index/main/docs/docs/examples/data/paul_graham/paul_graham_essay.txt",
        tf.name,
    )
    documents = SimpleDirectoryReader(input_files=[tf.name]).load_data()
llm = OpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo", temperature=0.1)
pipline = IngestionPipeline(
    transformations=[
        SentenceSplitter(chunk_size=2048, chunk_overlap=20),
        TitleExtractor(llm=llm, metadata_mode=MetadataMode.EMBED, num_workers=8),
        SummaryExtractor(llm=llm, metadata_mode=MetadataMode.EMBED, num_workers=8),
        OpenAIEmbedding(),
    ]
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    nodes = pipline.run(documents=documents)
    handler.print_trace_trees()

title: Correcting the behaviour of the constructor of llama_index.core.utils.GlobalsHelper
body:
# Description

###  Current behaviour
- `nltk.data.path` is extended to incorporate `_nltk_data_dir` which is then used in the lookups
- the lookups themselves(`nltk.data.find`) are invoked with a total override of the paths

The consequence: 
- the data present in default locations(as per nltk algorithm) is never attempted to be found there, but always downloaded, increasing the cost of the bootstrapping 

```
        if self._nltk_data_dir not in nltk.data.path:
            nltk.data.path.append(self._nltk_data_dir)  # <--- extending the nltk.data.path: OK

        # ensure access to data is there
        try:
            nltk.data.find("corpora/stopwords", paths=[self._nltk_data_dir]) # <--- completely ignoring current nltk.data.path: NOK
        except LookupError:
            nltk.download("stopwords", download_dir=self._nltk_data_dir)

        try:
            nltk.data.find("tokenizers/punkt", paths=[self._nltk_data_dir]) # <--- completely ignoring current nltk.data.path: NOK
        except LookupError:
            nltk.download("punkt", download_dir=self._nltk_data_dir)

```

### Proposal
- respecting defaults locations, adding the `_static/nltk_cache` as a fallback, to avoid unnecessary network round-trips.

Fixes # (issue)

title: Bind MongoDB primary key ID to Document object to ensure refresh_ref_docs only vectorizes changed data.
body:
Bind MongoDB primary key ID to Document object to ensure refresh_ref_docs only vectorizes changed data.

# Description

When creating Document objects from MongoDB data, bind the MongoDB primary key ID to the Document object. This ensures that the refresh_ref_docs method can verify if the current document already exists. Otherwise, each Document object read from MongoDB will have a different UUID, causing refresh_ref_docs to re-vectorize all data each time it is executed (since the hash value differs each time). Our use case involves reading all data from MongoDB and using refresh_ref_docs to vectorize only the data that has changed, rather than re-vectorizing all data each time.

At first, I thought the framework could automatically recognize which Documents had already been vectorized when I saw the comments for the refresh_ref_docs method. However, I later discovered that every time the refresh_ref_docs function is executed, all of my data is vectorized again. Upon examining the logic of this function, I found that when performing hash verification (self._docstore.get_document_hash), it uses the doc_id of the document object. This doc_id is generated by uuid by default, not my MongoDB primary key id. This caused the hash matching to always be false, leading the program to consider the document as new data and trigger a refresh. Therefore, when creating a Document object by reading MongoDB data, I bound the MongoDB primary key id to it. This finally resolved the issue of repeated vectorization.

def get_changed_docs(es_index_name: str, doc_list: List[Document]) -> List[Document]:
    es_client = get_es_client()
    changed_doc_list = []
    for doc in doc_list:
        query = {
            "query": {
                "match": {
                    "metadata.doc_id": f"{doc.get_doc_id()}"
                }
            }
        }
        result = es_client.search(index=es_index_name, body=query)

        if not result['hits']['hits']:
            changed_doc_list.append(doc)
            continue

        hits = result['hits']['hits']

        for hit in hits:
            node_content = hit['_source']['metadata']['_node_content']
            node_obj = json.loads(node_content)
            if node_obj['relationships']['1']['hash'] != doc.hash:
                changed_doc_list.append(doc)

    return changed_doc_list

title: 📝 Fix streaming example in "standalone usage" docs
body:
# Description

Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed. Please also include relevant motivation and context. List any dependencies that are required for this change.

The [LLM standalone usage docs](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/module_guides/models/llms/usage_standalone/) has an example for streaming:
```py
llm = OpenAI()
resp = llm.stream_complete("Paul Graham is ")
for delta in resp:
    print(delta, end="")
```

When `delta: CompletionResponse` is printed, its `.text` attribute instead of `.delta` is displayed. Text contains the concatenated streams of tokens returned thus far, while `.delta` contains only the latest token received from the LLM.

As a result when this line was run, instead of getting a token-by-token stream of:
```
a computer scientist, entrepreneur, and venture capitalist.
```

you'll get this long and jumbled output:
```
aa computera computer scientista computer scientist,a computer scientist, entrepreneura computer scientist, entrepreneur,a computer scientist, entrepreneur, anda computer scientist, entrepreneur, and venturea computer scientist, entrepreneur, and venture capitalista computer scientist, entrepreneur, and venture capitalist.
```

The intention was likely to use `.delta` attribute, and so this PR updates the example accordingly.

title: add delete_by_field method in RedisVectorStore
body:
# Description

The addition of the delete_by_field method provides more flexibility and functionality to the RedisVectorStore class compared to the previous delete method.  The delete method allows for deletion of nodes based on a specific document ID (ref_doc_id). This means that to delete a node, you must know its exact document ID. This can be limiting in situations where you want to delete nodes based on other criteria.  On the other hand, the delete_by_field method allows developers to delete nodes based on a specific field name and field value. This means you can delete nodes based on any field, not just the document ID. This is particularly useful when dealing with large amounts of data and needing to delete data based on specific conditions

title: Markdown parser that allows splitting of header contents
body:
# Description

This PR introduces an alternative markdown parser which allows more granular control over how a markdown document is split. In particular, it allows for setting a maximum node length. If the contents belonging to a header exceed the maximum node length, the contents are split into multiple parts. The header title is repeated in the next node, and the contents flow over into the new node, without overlap. More options could be added later. It may make sense to generalize the existing MarkdownSplitter class, instead of introducing this new class.

Using this alternative splitter has been integral to the success of our RAG-based LLM application. When a user has markdown documents information stored under headers, while some contents are short and others are long, the existing MarkdownSplitter may not always suffice. For example, in our use case, using the MarkdownSplitter led to token limit being exceeded for creating the embeddings for long sections of text. Also, including large chunks of texts in the context using RAG can unnecessarily increase latency and costs, while a more granular approach would have obtained similar quality of LLM output. We are dealing with many documents, which are generated on a repeated basis, so adding more headers in the raw documents is too time-consuming.

I am sharing this code as others may experience similar scenarios.

NOTE: I still have to clean up this code, so at this point I'm looking for feedback on whether the idea is something that LlamaIndex would like to consider for merging. If there are plans to merge this, I will spend the effort to refactor the code and implement other feedback.

Fixes # (issue)

# Description

I went through the tutorial https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/latest/examples/property_graph/property_graph_advanced/
focusing on the nebula option.

This PR suggests some minor fixes.

In addition, I wanted to report on some troubles I ran into.

- The Nebula DB needs to be created prior to the lines:

```python
graph_store = NebulaPropertyGraphStore(
    space="llamaindex_nebula_property_graph", overwrite=True
)
```

The creation can be done with `jupyter-nebulagraph` as shown later in the tutorial or with an external tool like [`nebula-console`](https://docs.nebula-graph.io/3.8.0/nebula-console/).

```
CREATE SPACE IF NOT EXISTS llamaindex_nebula_property_graph(vid_type=FIXED_STRING(256));
```

- Incidentally, I ran into [the error that a VID was too large to fit](https://docs.nebula-graph.io/3.8.0/20.appendix/0.FAQ/#how_to_resolve_the_error_the_vid_must_be_a_64-bit_integer_or_a_string_fitting_space_vertex_id_length_limit), so I think it would be good to filter the `params[all_id]` in [nebula_property_graph](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/main/llama-index-integrations/graph_stores/llama-index-graph-stores-nebula/llama_index/graph_stores/nebula/nebula_property_graph.py)

- I debugged for a long time why no results where ever returned! The work around was to set the `max_new_tokens` to a really high value, so that the JSON has a chance to be complete. If the JSON is partial, there is a silent parsing error in [def `_aextract` of function `schema_llm.py`](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/8bf9d7a7243750e8b5f8a1d77328b883e13c9baf/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/indices/property_graph/transformations/schema_llm.py#L300).

Maybe just a pointer to the [guide](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/latest/module_guides/indexing/lpg_index_guide/#saving-tofrom-disk). Incidentally, it's important to say that the default instructions will NOT work, one needs to follow the [next section](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/latest/module_guides/indexing/lpg_index_guide/#saving-and-loading-with-integrations). title: LanceDB: removed mode from the add statement since mode should be append
body:
Really small update to remove the `mode` option from the lancedb `add` statement since it was sharing the mode option with `create_table`, and I think the wrapper was intending it mainly for create_table.  Two issues with sharing the mode with `add`:

1. The options for mode are different for `add` than they are for `create_table`: for add, the valid values are "append" and "overwrite" whereas for `create_table` they are "create" and "overwrite". 

2. There is an unintended behavior when the value "overwrite" is specified for mode and is shared by the two methods: it will always overwrite the table thereby not allow you to build up the vector database with new embeddings.  

Removing the `mode` from `add` reverts the value to it's default which is "append", which should be what most situations will warrant.  Alternatively, there could be a separate parameter to control the mode for add, but it really doesn't seem necessary.

title: Add metadata for DatabaseReader
body:
# Description

**Add Metadata Functionality to DatabaseReader**
In the original implementation, the DatabaseReader loaded all the data into text format. However, sometimes we don't need to retrieve all the columns; we only need some fields as metadata. Therefore, I have updated the load_data method.

With this update, we can now load data from the database and specify certain fields to be included as metadata. Here a simple example:
```python
from llama_index.readers.database import DatabaseReader

reader = DatabaseReader(uri="sqlite:///D:/AAA/BBB/msg.db?table=msg")

# load data from database
documents = reader.load_data(
    query="SELECT msgid, content, sender, timestamp FROM msg", 
    doc_cols=["content"],
    metadata_cols=["msgid", "sender", "timestamp"], 
)
```

~~Fixes # (issue)~~

title: Add code to handle hallucinated function names
body:
# Description

When using tools with our agents, it is possible for an LLM to hallucinate the name of a tool (e.g., the LLM requests a function whose name doesn't match any specified). Currently, llama-index raises an exception, and so ends the interaction. In this change, I've modified our `get_function_by_name` to avoid raising an exception in this case, and instead return `None`. All agents that call this method now construct a message asking the LLM to double check the name. I've also done a significant amount of refactoring (asyncio stuff, duplicated code), which helps facilitate these new changes.

Fixes #13649, #13484, #12483, #12479

body: ## Issue Sub-spans delegated to threads cannot find its parent. For example, this can happen here: https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/56a0e70607115eaac3d79b1fd90d9478a871d228/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/chat_engine/simple.py#L122-L124 Furthermore, in the thread shown above, the following event fires with a `span_id` from outside the thread, but the outside span may no longer be open when the event fires (when streaming is done). https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/56a0e70607115eaac3d79b1fd90d9478a871d228/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/llms/callbacks.py#L97-L98 ## Before Sub-spans delegated to threads are separated from parent span, resulting in multiple traces. ## After Sub-spans can now find their correct `parent_span_id`. ## Original Behavior The original behavior was captured in [this notebook](https://github.com/RogerHYang/llama_index/blob/f8e48c8ea481e5bb3b291e65c8c2eb20b7fb41d7/docs/docs/examples/instrumentation/basic_usage.ipynb?short_path=bbd64b0#L618). ## Code Below is code producing the screenshots above. ```python import tempfile from urllib.request import urlretrieve from llama_index.core import Settings, SimpleDirectoryReader, VectorStoreIndex from llama_index.core.instrumentation import get_dispatcher from llama_index.core.instrumentation.span_handlers import SimpleSpanHandler from llama_index.llms.openai import OpenAI handler = SimpleSpanHandler() dispatcher = get_dispatcher() dispatcher.add_span_handler(handler) with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() as tf: urlretrieve( "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/run-llama/llama_index/main/docs/docs/examples/data/paul_graham/paul_graham_essay.txt", tf.name, ) documents = SimpleDirectoryReader(input_files=[tf.name]).load_data() index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(documents) Settings.llm = OpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo") if __name__ == "__main__": query_engine = index.as_chat_engine() response_stream = query_engine.stream_chat("What did the author do growing up?") response_stream.print_response_stream() handler.print_trace_trees() ```

title: Bugfix: Use aiter_lines function to iterate over lines in ollama integration
body:
# Description

The ollama integration uses the function `aiter_text` to iterate over text chunks returned by ollama and decodes the chunk as a json object.  
This code fails if the json payload is big enough that the line containing the json string is split over two (or more) chunks as the code tries (and fails) to decode a partial json object.

This change changes the function used to `aiter_lines` which parses the returned chunks into individual lines and returns those instead.

See https://www.python-httpx.org/api/#response for the documentation and https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/master/httpx/_models.py#L962 for the implementation of the `aiter_lines` function

title: Deprecate mode() in favor of __init__(base_url=...) for NVIDIA, NVIDIAEmbedding, NVIDIARerank
body:
# Description

To simplify and align switching from hosted and local backends, the `mode()` method is deprecated in favor of using `base_url` passed to constructors.

The `mode()` method will be removed in v0.2.

Old usage -
```
from llama_index.llms.nvidia import NVIDIA
from llama_index.embeddings.nvidia import NVIDIA Embedding
from llama_index.postprocessor.nvidia_rerank import NVIDIARerank

llm = NVIDIA().mode("nim", base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1")
embedder = NVIDIAEmbedding().mode("nim", base_url="http://localhost:12345/v1")
ranker = NVIDIARerank().mode("nim", base_url="http://localhost:1976/v1")
```

New usage -
```
from llama_index.llms.nvidia import NVIDIA
from llama_index.embeddings.nvidia import NVIDIA Embedding
from llama_index.postprocessor.nvidia_rerank import NVIDIARerank

llm = NVIDIA(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1")
embedder = NVIDIAEmbedding(base_url="http://localhost:12345/v1")
ranker = NVIDIARerank(base_url="http://localhost:1976/v1")
```

A full documentation refresh will follow. I want to get the deprecation warnings to users ASAP.

title: [Core] Omni-Modal Embedding, Vector Index and Retriever
body:
# Description

This PR lays the groundwork for extending the multi-modal support to other modalities (such as audio). The main components of this PR are:

- [`Modality`](https://github.com/DarkLight1337/llama_index/blob/omni-modal/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/embeddings/omni_modal_base.py#L172): Encapsulates the embedding-agnostic information about each modality
    - e.g.: how to read `BaseNode` and `QueryBundle`s that belong to that modality.
- [`OmniModalEmbedding`](https://github.com/DarkLight1337/llama_index/blob/omni-modal/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/embeddings/omni_modal_base.py#L481): Base class for Embedding component that supports any modality, not just text and image.
    - Concrete subclasses should define the supported `document_modalities` and `query_modalities`, and implement `_get_embedding` (and related methods) for those modalities accordingly.
- [`OmniModalEmbeddingBundle`](https://github.com/DarkLight1337/llama_index/blob/omni-modal/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/embeddings/omni_modal_base.py#L961): Composite of `OmniModalEmbedding` where multiple embedding models can be combined together.
    - To avoid ambiguity, only one model per document modality is allowed.
    - There can be multiple models per query modality (each covering a different document modality).
- [`OmniModalVectorStoreIndex`](https://github.com/DarkLight1337/llama_index/blob/omni-modal/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/indices/omni_modal/base.py#L40): Index component that stores documents using `OmniModalEmbeddingBundle`. It is meant to be a drop-in replacement for `MultiModalVectorStoreIndex`.
    - There is no need to specify the document modality when storing `BaseNode`s. The modality is inferred automatically based on the class type.
    - **Note:** To load a persisted index, use `OmniModalVectorStoreIndex.load_from_storage` instead of `llama_index.core.load_index_from_storage`, since we do not serialize the details of each modality.
- [`OmniModalVectorIndexRetriever`](https://github.com/DarkLight1337/llama_index/blob/omni-modal/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/indices/omni_modal/retriever.py#L62): Retriever component that queries documents using `OmniModalEmbeddingBundle`.
    - You can set top-k for each document modality.
    - You must specify the query modality when passing in the `QueryBundle`. (May be changed in the future to automatically detect the modality in a manner similar to the case for document nodes)
    - You can specify one or more document modalities to retrieve from, which may be different from the query modality.

As you may have guessed, I took inspiration from the recently released `GPT-4o` (where "o" stands for "omni") when naming these components, to distinguish from the existing `MultiModal*` components for text-image retrieval. I am open to other naming suggestions.

This change intentionally leaves the existing code untouched at the expense of some code duplication. Future PRs may work on the following:

- Replace the existing `BaseEmbedding` class with `OmniModalEmbedding` (since it's more general).
- Integrate the function of extracting document/query data based on `Modality` into existing `BaseNode` and `QueryBundle` classes. That way, we can replace `Modality` with a string key which can be serialized and deserialized easily.
